model_text_2018.table: 2018 IBC Table 2902.1 (read on UpCodes, 'Mississippi Building Code 2018'): restaurants, banquet halls and food courts 1 per 75 male and 1 per 75 female; business 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50; educational 1 per 50. The same ratios as the state pack's 2024 rows, so the state pack's worked examples stand: office 1/1, 2/2, 3/3, 5/5; restaurant 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 3/3; school 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 4/4 at 50/100/200/400 occupants.
model_text_2018.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 [...] To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex.
model_text_2018.separate_rooms: 2018 IBC 2902.2 exceptions as read: dwelling and sleeping units; structures or tenant spaces with 15 or fewer occupants in total; mercantile occupancies with 100 or fewer; business occupancies with 25 or fewer. No exception for multi-user rooms for all persons.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Jackson job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Mississippi humidity and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Jackson offices, schools, hospitals and government buildings, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes everywhere. Mississippi has no separate modern state access code, and the model building rules Jackson has adopted bring their own access standard with them.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** the model building rules Jackson has adopted require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Jackson's building rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Mississippi extras:** the access standard in Jackson's building rules asks for one thing in a wheelchair stall that the federal standard doesn't: an upright grab bar on the side wall as well as the horizontal one. An older state law also sets stall sizes for buildings paid for with public money and has the State Board of Health review the plans. Ask the Building Permits Division which standard it enforces.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under the model building rules Jackson has adopted, a one-person restroom is marked for use by either sex and counts toward the required toilets. Men and women need separate rooms, except in a building designed for 15 people or fewer, an office for 25 or fewer or a shop for 100 or fewer. That edition has no provision for a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask the Building Permits Division before planning one. Mississippi law requires public schools, community colleges and public universities to have restrooms designated for females and for males, or one-person rooms.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Jackson requires a permit to construct, enlarge, repair, move or demolish a building. The model rules it has adopted exempt "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. They don't name toilet partitions, and Jackson adopted them with its own amendments. Ask the Building Permits Division whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Mississippi has no single statewide building code, so the model building rules Jackson has adopted decide. They count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to two thirds of the toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: Jackson adopted these rules with its own amendments, so confirm the count with the Building Permits Division. These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the model rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Building Permits Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Commercial general contractors register with Jackson's building official, show their Mississippi license before a permit is issued, and carry liability insurance. Mississippi requires a state contractor license for commercial jobs of $50,000 or more, including subcontracts. Confirm what your project needs with Jackson's Building Permits Division. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor on a commercial job of $50,000 or more in Mississippi needs a state contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Mississippi has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work. For a carpenter on building work in Hinds County the federal rate is $15.33 an hour plus $4.42 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% state. Jackson adds 1% on goods sold from a business located in the city, which makes 8% there. Goods delivered into Jackson by a seller outside the city don't carry the extra 1%. Mississippi has no county sales tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, colleges and state office buildings:** stalls that stand up to heavy daily traffic, in a finish that matches the building's standard.
